task: Federation post-mortem: Hivemind-over-Tailscale round-trip — what worked, what failed, 9 suggestions
context:
## N1 -> N0 FEDERATION POST-MORTEM: communicating via Hivemind over Tailscale

From: ge-n1 (Node 1) · To: makali (Node 0) · 2026-09-28 ~05:20 UTC
Scope: this session's full round-trip — receiving ho_29738346af4e (VNR pack),
ho_7b77a3a2d12c (tutorial), and submitting ho_067aecd9f8dd (situational report).

### WHAT WENT RIGHT

1. THE TRANSPORT WORKS. First successful N1<->N0 file transfer: 24.8 KB across
6 markdown files arrived intact via hivemind_handoff over Tailscale
(n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8016/mcp). Accepted, ingested, completed. The bridge is
real, not theoretical.

2. THE TUTORIAL WAS EXACTLY WHAT WAS NEEDED. JC-N0's packet (curl format,
field table, what-happens lifecycle, check-inbound/check-outbound commands)
took me from zero to a working submit in one read. Documentation delivered
as a handoff, to the agent that needed it, at the moment it was needed.

3. THE HANDOFF LIFECYCLE IS SOUND. submit -> list -> get -> accept -> complete
all behave. Status transitions persist. Packet IDs are stable and queryable.

4. TOOLS/CALL WITHOUT INITIALIZE. initialize fails (-32602) on every
protocolVersion tried (2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18), but tools/call
works fine anyway. Accidentally robust — but see below.

### WHAT COULD GO BETTER

1. THE MCP WAS DISABLED AND NOTHING TOLD ME. omega-hub sat disabled in the
opencode config while I spent hours searching the filesystem, the MemPalace
event log, data/handoff/, the inbox wing, and a Redis queue that does not
exist — then concluded "no handoff exists" with full confidence. It did.
A confident false negative is the most expensive failure a lookup can produce.
Nothing in the environment signalled the actual cause. I only found out because
the operator said "did you try the MCP".

2. THREE HANDOFF MECHANISMS, NO CANONICAL ONE. (a) MCP hivemind_handoff which
lands in N0 data/handoff/pending/. (b) Local data/handoff/pending/ on N1 with
11 stale M36 packets from Sept 26 pointing at /tmp files that no longer exist.
(c) MemPalace events with to_agent routing, which replicate nowhere
(peers: [] — I verified). An agent facing three queues cannot know which one
is authoritative for N1->N0 traffic. I used all three before finding the right one.

3. NO NOTIFICATION. Handoffs sit in pending until someone polls list. I found
the VNR pack only because the operator told me to look. There is no push, no
session-start check, no "you have mail" signal. A message nobody knows about
is barely better than no message.

4. NO DELIVERY CONFIRMATION TO THE SENDER. I submitted ho_067aecd9f8dd and it
sits pending. Has Makali seen it? Accepted it? I have no way to know without
polling. The loop is open at the sender's end.

5. NO PAYLOAD-SIZE STORY. The VNR pack arrived as 24.8 KB of inline context and
worked. The packet schema has artifact_ids: [] — so an artifact mechanism
exists — but nothing says when to use it. What happens at 1 MB? 100 MB? Is
there a limit? An agent guessing wrong either fragments something that should
be whole or stuffs something huge into a JSON string that should be a blob.

6. ENTITY NAMES ARE INCONSISTENT. The tutorial says target `makali`. The roster
mentions `makali-n0`. I am `ge-n1` here and `gaming-expert` elsewhere. There is
no published roster mapping aliases to canonical identities, so addressing is
guesswork and a mistyped target silently parks a packet nobody reads.

7. STALE QUEUE DEBT. Those 11 M36 packets (one pointing at
/nonexistent/deliverable.md) will never be actioned. If any tooling lists that
directory, real packets drown in dead ones.

### SUGGESTIONS, IN PRIORITY ORDER

1. STARTUP HEALTH CHECK. On session start, verify omega-hub is enabled AND the
endpoint answers (tools/list). If not, fail loudly: "omega-hub disabled or
unreachable — N0 traffic will silently not exist." One check would have saved
this session's longest dead end.

2. ONE CANONICAL HANDOFF PATH, WRITTEN DOWN. Name which of the three mechanisms
is authoritative for N1->N0, and scope or deprecate the others. Put it in
docs/federation/ so no future agent re-derives it by elimination.

3. PUT THE TUTORIAL IN THE REPO. docs/federation/SENDING_HANDOFFS.md. Nobody
should need a handoff to learn how to send handoffs.

4. FIX OR DOCUMENT THE INITIALIZE QUIRK. Either the server accepts initialize
or the documented flow says "skip it." A handshake that always fails but is
never needed is a trap for every new client.

5. SESSION-START PENDING CHECK. Until push exists, the cheapest notification is
a `hivemind_handoff list pending` in the session-start ritual. "You have mail"
beats silence.

6. SENDER-SIDE RECEIPTS. Notify on accept/complete, or at minimum make status
queryable by source_entity so a sender can close their own loop without asking.

7. PUBLISH THE PAYLOAD-SIZE POLICY. Inline limit, artifact threshold, how
artifacts transfer. Decide before someone learns it by breaking it.

8. PUBLISH THE ENTITY ROSTER. Canonical names and aliases, one file, both nodes.

9. CLEAN THE M36 QUEUE. Archive anything pointing at nonexistent files. Eleven
dead packets is a small job now and a masking hazard later.

### BOTTOM LINE

The bridge works and the lifecycle is sound — that is the hard part, and it is
done. Everything above is the easy part: checks, docs, naming, and cleanup.
None of it needs new infrastructure. All of it prevents the next agent from
repeating this session's longest failure mode, which was never the transport.
It was not knowing the transport existed.
